_meta.description: Live macro themes affecting currencies but not on the scheduled news calendar. Update as regime-changing events happen. Scanner reads this at brief generation time and displays it in the daily/weekly review.
_meta.howToUse: Each theme should include: (1) short title, (2) start date, (3) currency implications with brief reasoning, (4) a specific watchLevel that would invalidate the theme, (5) affectedPairs for scanner correlation. Retire themes by moving to _retired[] with an endDate.

themes.title: Canada-US trade war escalating — Sep 8 retaliatory tariffs LIVE; Trump counter-escalates barring Canadian goods from federal contracts; BoC holds 2.25% with hawkish inflation tilt; Jan 1 2027 50% auto tariff threat structural
themes.summary: As of September 9, the Canada-US trade war has escalated beyond the Sep 8 binary event with a new US counter-move. Canada's C$27.6 billion, 700+ tariff-line retaliatory package — rates of 15%, 25%, and 50% matched dollar-for-dollar to US Section 338 and Section 232 tariffs, including doubling steel and aluminum duties to 50% — took effect at 12:01 a.m. September 8 as scheduled. Then, at approximately 20:39 UTC on September 8, President Trump announced he would direct US federal agencies to remove Canadian-origin products from government contracts, adding a new non-tariff escalation lever that markets had not priced. The tit-for-tat sequence continues with no diplomatic off-ramp visible. USDCAD on September 8 traded near 1.3803, materially below the 1.3900 area targeted in prior analysis, as two offsetting forces capped USD upside: oil surging above $97/barrel (WTI, driven by ongoing US-Iran tension in the Strait of Hormuz) provided a commodity tailwind for CAD, and Canadian August employment collapsed -41,700 vs expectations of +15,000 — a miss that reinforces BoC dovish risk but also signals tariff damage is hitting the real economy. The Bank of Canada held its policy rate at 2.25% at its September 2 meeting as widely expected, but flagged increased inflation risks from tariffs while acknowledging the growth outlook had become more uncertain — a mildly hawkish hold that prevents aggressive BoC easing expectations from crushing CAD further. Five-bank consensus forecasts place USDCAD at 1.37 in Q4 2026 with the clearest downside risk to that forecast being further US-Canada escalation — the Trump federal-contracts ban on Sep 8 evening is exactly that downside risk materializing. Trump's structural Jan 1, 2027 threat of 50% tariffs on all Canadian autos, trucks, parts, and steel remains the medium-term CAD overhang. The absence of any diplomatic channel and both governments' public commitments make de-escalation structurally difficult in the near term.

implications.CAD: MAXIMUM CAD negative — US 50% Section 338 tariffs live since Aug 22, Canada's full 700+ line dollar-for-dollar retaliation live since Sep 8, Trump Sep 8 evening counter-escalated by barring Canadian goods from federal contracts, no diplomatic off-ramp, Jan 1 2027 50% auto tariff threat adds structural overhang. USDCAD ~1.3803 on Sep 8, held lower than expected by oil above $97 (CAD positive via energy export channel). Canadian Aug employment -41,700 (vs +15k expected) signals real tariff damage — BoC held 2.25% Sep 2 with hawkish inflation tilt but growth uncertainty limits rate hike enthusiasm. USDCAD directional bias remains long on any oil pullback. BoC Oct 28 meeting is the next policy binary.
implications.USD: USDCAD directionally bullish from tariff war but oil above $97 is a temporary CAD support partially capping USDCAD upside. Fed hike odds (54% hold, 46% hike per Kalshi Sep 9) are a secondary USD driver — Sep 11 CPI and Sep 15-16 FOMC will set the USD cross-rate trajectory.
implications.MXN: USMCA credibility damage from US-Canada rupture keeps uncertainty elevated for Mexico as well. Divergence in US-Mexico vs US-Canada bilateral progress adds uncertainty premium.
implications.EUR: Indirect — EURCAD likely bid on CAD weakness. Broader protectionism signal from Section 338 invocation has limited but non-zero EUR contagion.
implications.AUD: Commodity-bloc contagion — AUD partially insulated by high oil/copper prices but trades defensively in acute CAD-shock episodes. AUDUSD subject to cross-currents: oil/commodity support vs tariff-war risk-off and post-Warsh USD strength.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDCAD vol elevated. NZD defensive in commodity-bloc risk-off episodes.
implications.GBP: GBPCAD directional trade on CAD weakness. GBP otherwise dominated by BoE path and USD dynamics.
implications.JPY: CADJPY lower on dual pressure: CAD structural weakness from Section 338 tariff war plus structural JPY bid from BOJ Sep 17-18 hike cycle now 84% priced.

themes.watchLevel: USDCAD 1.3803 is the Sep 8 close — oil above $97 (Iran conflict) is the key CAD support factor partially offsetting tariff-war USD bid. Key levels: 1.3900 remains the upside target and psychological resistance — a clean daily close above 1.3900 opens 1.4017-1.4100 and becomes achievable on any oil pullback from $97. 1.3776 (Sep 8 session low) is immediate support; a sustained break below 1.3750 requires either a diplomatic surprise or oil above $100 sustained. Trump's Sep 8 federal-contracts ban is the new escalation to watch: if Washington follows with additional non-tariff measures (export controls, financial restrictions) USDCAD accelerates above 1.39-1.40 regardless of oil. BoC Oct 28 next binary. Theme ends only on: (1) formal re-opening of US-Canada talks with credible framework, or (2) Trump executive action suspending Section 338.

themes.title: USDJPY at 6-month low ~154.60 — BOJ Sep 17-18 hike 84% priced on Japan wage/GDP beat Sep 8; FOMC Sep 15-16 arrives 48hrs before; dual central bank binary week is NOW
themes.summary: As of September 9, USDJPY has extended its collapse to approximately 154.60-154.70, a six-month low, driven by a powerful Sep 8 catalyst: strong overnight Japanese wage growth and GDP data beat expectations, pushing overnight index swap pricing of a Bank of Japan hike at the Sep 17-18 meeting to approximately 84% — up sharply from 73% as of September 2. The pair's range on September 8 was 154.56 to 156.28, with the move down roughly 1% on the session. The trajectory since the Sep 2 peak at 160.33 is now approximately 570 pips of JPY strength in seven sessions, a historically large move driven by three reinforcing pillars: (1) intervention regime credibility — the 160.00 level was rejected cleanly and the pair has never recovered; (2) BOJ hawkish data flow — Japan wage and GDP beats on Sep 8 joined Governor Ueda's Sep 1 G20 signal and board member Takata's Sep 2 Sapporo comments calling for nimble hikes, with 2-year JGB yields at multi-decade highs; (3) US-Japan policy coordination confirmed — Bessent-Ueda bilateral at G20 Asheville and Treasury Secretary Bessent's public statements stressing decisive action on yen weakness. BOJ sources (Reuters) confirmed the central bank is set to raise rates as early as September to 1.25% and is considering accelerating the pace of tightening beyond the prior twice-yearly cadence. The dual central bank binary week is now imminent: the FOMC meets September 15-16 with an updated SEP and dot plot, followed immediately by the BOJ September 17-18 meeting. A scenario in which both central banks hike within 48 hours of each other — FOMC to 3.75-4.00% and BOJ to 1.25% — would represent an extraordinary USDJPY volatility event, with the initial FOMC USD bid likely overwhelmed by the subsequent BOJ JPY bid. Elevated oil prices and Hormuz-related safe-haven demand add further complexity. The September 11 US CPI report (two days away) remains the final major swing variable before both decisions.

implications.JPY: Three-pillar structural JPY support fully dominating: (1) Intervention regime — 160.00 rejected, USDJPY now ~154.60, 570-pip collapse from Sep 2 peak; (2) BOJ Sep 17-18 hike 84% priced on Japan wage/GDP beat Sep 8, Ueda and Takata both hawkish, Reuters sources confirm rate hike as early as September; (3) Bessent-Ueda bilateral confirmed US-Japan policy coordination. Sep 11 US CPI could temporarily revive USD demand. Sep 15-16 FOMC hike (46% probability per Kalshi) could provide a short-squeeze before BOJ. Sep 17-18 BOJ is the dominant binary.
implications.USD: USDJPY has lost ~570 pips since Sep 2 as BOJ hike narrative overwhelmed carry. Kalshi shows Sep FOMC at 46% hike / 54% hold — the FOMC outcome is genuinely uncertain. Sep 11 CPI is the USD's last chance to reassert before the BOJ binary overwhelms the pair. Rate differential direction of travel is decisively USD-negative vs JPY from BOJ side over medium term.
implications.EUR: EURJPY under pressure from BOJ hike pricing at 84%. Multi-decade high JGB yields narrowing EUR-JPY rate differential structurally.
implications.GBP: GBPJPY under dual intervention and carry-unwind pressure — Sep 8 yen surge hit all JPY crosses sharply.
implications.CHF: CHFJPY lower on intervention pressure. SNB in easing mode.
implications.CAD: CADJPY lower on dual pressure: CAD structural weakness from Section 338 tariff war plus JPY structural bid from BOJ 84% hike pricing.
implications.AUD: AUDJPY under intervention and carry-unwind pressure — dropped sharply Sep 8 alongside USDJPY. Softer domestic AUD data (per Sep 8 reports) adds independent AUD headwind.
implications.NZD: Same dynamic as AUD. NZDJPY under intervention and carry-unwind pressure.

themes.watchLevel: USDJPY ~154.60-154.70 is the Sep 8 close — six-month low after 570-pip collapse from 160.33. Key support: 154.56 (Sep 8 intraday low); a break below 154.00 signals further JPY strength toward 152-150. Key resistance: 156.28 (Sep 8 high); a recovery above 156.50-157.00 without new BOJ/MoF pushback = carry traders re-engaging and partial unwind of hike pricing. Sep 11 CPI binary: hot (core above 0.3% MoM) = USD short-squeeze, USDJPY could bounce to 156-157 temporarily before BOJ meeting; soft = USDJPY continues toward 153-152. BOJ Sep 17-18 is the hard binary with 84% hike priced: hike to 1.25% = USDJPY likely drops toward 150-148, 2yr JGB yields rally sharply; no hike = JPY sells off sharply, 157-160 re-test, intervention regime faces fresh stress. FOMC Sep 15-16 hike arriving 48hrs before BOJ = maximum two-way volatility scenario. USDJPY below 153.00 = BOJ hike confirmed and JPY structural bull trend extended. Any MoF/Bessent statement disclaiming further intervention = theme ends immediately.

themes.title: Fed Sep 15-16 FOMC binary — hike odds 46% (Kalshi) narrowed from 68%; Sep 11 CPI final tiebreaker; PCE 3.7%, core CPI elevated; dual central bank week Sep 15-18 (FOMC+BOJ) NOW imminent
themes.summary: As of September 9, the Warsh hawkish repricing from Jackson Hole (August 28 keynote) remains structurally intact but September hike probability has narrowed since August payrolls. Kalshi, as of September 9, shows the Fed maintains rate at 46 cents vs hike at 55 cents — implying approximately 54% hold, 46% hike — a notable tightening from the 65-68% hike probability shown by CME FedWatch as of August 31. Polymarket still prices 60-65% odds of a 25bp move at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting, reflecting genuine market split. The FOMC meets September 15-16 (not September 16 standalone as in prior update) with an updated Summary of Economic Projections and dot plot. Chair Warsh described PCE at 3.7% and core measures as 'concerning' at Jackson Hole, while noting the 6-month PCE change at 4.1% — well above the 2% target. Persistent headline CPI at 3.4% year-over-year in July with energy still elevated from Middle East supply shocks, and unemployment steady at 4.1%, have kept hike probability meaningful. August nonfarm payrolls printed 162,000 — about three times consensus — reinforcing labor market resilience. The July FOMC vote was 9-3 to hold with dissenters from Cleveland, Minneapolis, and Dallas all pushing for a hike — the most dissents since September 2016. The September 11 August CPI release is the critical final swing variable: a hot print (core above 0.3% MoM or YoY above 3.3%) revives hike probability toward 70%+ and validates DXY upside; a soft print (core at or below 0.2% MoM) collapses hike odds toward 35-40% and drives DXY lower. The September 15-16 FOMC arrives with updated SEP and dot plot 48 hours before the BOJ September 17-18 meeting — this dual central bank week is the highest-volatility FX event cluster of 2026. Oil above $97/barrel (WTI) adds a supply-side inflation upside risk that keeps the case for hiking alive even if CPI prints in-line.

implications.USD: DXY holding post-Warsh hawkish gains, 10yr UST near 4.79%. Kalshi Sep 9 shows 46% hike / 54% hold — the coin flip has shifted slightly toward hold since Aug 31. Sep 11 August CPI is the critical pre-FOMC tiebreaker: hot (core above 0.3% MoM or YoY above 3.3%) = hike odds back above 65-70%, DXY targets 100.50-101.00, EURUSD toward 1.1350; soft (core at or below 0.2% MoM) = hike odds drop to 35-40%, DXY retraces toward 98.50-99.00, EURUSD relief toward 1.1600+. Sep 15-16 FOMC with updated SEP/dot plot is the hard policy binary. Oil at $97 is an upside inflation wildcard.
implications.JPY: Warsh FOMC outcome creates cross-current against BOJ Sep hike narrative at 84%. USDJPY at 154.60 — the dual Sep 15-18 week means FOMC and BOJ land within 48 hours, creating maximum two-way USDJPY volatility. A Sep 15-16 FOMC hike to 3.75-4.00% followed by a Sep 17-18 BOJ hike to 1.25% is the extraordinary simultaneous-tightening scenario: initial USDJPY rally on FOMC, then sharp JPY surge on BOJ.
implications.EUR: EURUSD ~1.1500-1.1550 after retracing from 1.1657 on Warsh hawkish repricing. Sep 11 US CPI and Sep 15-16 FOMC are the next major EURUSD catalysts. ECB dynamics provide partial offset — ECB expected to hold.
implications.GBP: GBPUSD subject to post-Warsh USD strength. BoE's own path and UK fiscal discipline (Finance Minister Healey Sep 7 comments cited) are independent GBP drivers.
implications.CAD: Post-Warsh USD strength adds a second tailwind to USDCAD alongside the Section 338 tariff shock. BoC held 2.25% Sep 2 with hawkish inflation tilt — US-Canada rate differential remains USD-supportive. Sep 11 CPI is a dual USDCAD catalyst.
implications.AUD: AUDUSD reversed from multi-month highs on Warsh hawkish USD repricing. Softer domestic AUD data (Sep 8 reports noted) adds AUD-specific headwind. Sep 11 CPI is a dual AUD catalyst.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDUSD retraced from recent highs on Warsh USD bid. RBNZ dynamics provide independent NZD input.
implications.CHF: USDCHF lifted by Warsh hawkish repricing. SNB easing mode limits CHF upside. CHF safe-haven bid provides partial offset.

themes.watchLevel: Sep 11 August CPI is the critical pre-FOMC tiebreaker (2 days away): hot (core above 0.3% MoM or YoY above 3.3%) = hike odds back to 65-70%, DXY toward 100.50-101.00, EURUSD toward 1.1350; soft (core at or below 0.2% MoM) = hike odds collapse to 35-40%, DXY retraces toward 98.50-99.00. Sep 15-16 FOMC with updated SEP/dot plot is the hard policy binary: hike 25bps to 3.75-4.00% = full hawkish validation (Kalshi currently pricing 46% chance), DXY toward 101-102, EURUSD below 1.1300; hold with hawkish dots (2026 median above 4.00%) = partial validation; hold with unchanged dots = sell-the-news USD weakness. FOMC Sep 15-16 arrives 48hrs before BOJ Sep 17-18 — simultaneous hike from both central banks is the maximum USDJPY volatility scenario (initial USD bid, then massive JPY bid). 10yr UST at 4.79% is a key level — sustained move above 4.85% signals Sep hike plus Dec hike being discounted. DXY closing and sustaining below 98.00 = Warsh hawkish read fully unwound. Oil at $97 (US-Iran, Hormuz) is an upside inflation wildcard that keeps the hike case alive even on an in-line CPI print.
